item.title: Tuinakauvadra eager to return after injury-hit
item.description: Defending Wallaroos Player of the Year Tabua Tuinakauvadra is relishing her return to camp as she works her way back to full fitness. The number eight has joined the Wallaroos in the UK ahead of Saturday’s clash against defending World Cup champions England in Manchester.
item.content:encoded:
Defending Wallaroos Player of the Year Tabua Tuinakauvadra is relishing her return to camp as she works her way back to full fitness.

The number eight has joined the Wallaroos in the UK ahead of Saturday’s clash against defending World Cup champions England in Manchester.

After an injury-hit 2026 season, Tuinakauvadra is targeting the matches against France and Scotland as an ideal opportunity to return to action.

The powerhouse backrower tore the meniscus in her right knee at the start of the year, ruling her out of the Pacific Four series.

She eventually returned for Super Rugby W, but suffered a low-grade MCL injury in her other knee after returning to club rugby.

Tuinakauvadra says the injuries forced her to reassess her goals for the year.

The Wallaroos star has spent much of the year watching from the sidelines and is eager to return to the field.

She says she had particularly missed the opportunity to play and build on last year’s progress.

The Wallaroos have returned to Manchester, where they were based at the start of last year’s Rugby World Cup.

A full crowd is expected at CorpAcq Stadium for Saturday’s clash with England, where Australia will look to build on their previous success at the venue after recording a 73-0 win over Samoa, their biggest victory in World Cup history.

item.title: Four former footballers to receive education assistance for their children through Veterans Tournament
item.description: Four deserving former footballers will again receive assistance towards their children’s education through the RC Manubhai/Apco Coatings Veterans Tournament this year. Fiji Football Association CEO Mohammed Yusuf says the tournament has been held for the past 12 years and provides former district representatives with an opportunity to reunite, stay active and maintain their fitness.
item.content:encoded:
Four deserving former footballers will again receive assistance towards their children’s education through the RC Manubhai/Apco Coatings Veterans Tournament this year.

Fiji Football Association CEO Mohammed Yusuf says the tournament has been held for the past 12 years and provides former district representatives with an opportunity to reunite, stay active and maintain their fitness.

Speaking during the pool draws at the Fiji FA Academy in Vatuwaqa, Yusuf says the education assistance initiative, which has been running for the past seven years, is part of the tournament’s ongoing focus on the welfare of former players.

Yusuf says Fiji FA does not take any profit from the tournament, and proceeds generated from sponsorship and registration fees are channelled back into supporting the welfare of former players.

The tournament will be held from this Friday to Sunday in Ba, with matches at the Four R Stadium at Govind Park and the Fiji FA Academy grounds.

A total of 15 teams have been confirmed, with nine competing in the Over-40 division and six in the Over-50 division.

Yusuf says the tournament brings together players who have represented their district teams and have now retired or are nearing retirement.

He says it also provides an opportunity for families to get involved while promoting the well-being of veteran players.

Fiji FA has also revealed plans to expand the tournament next year to three age categories - Over-40, Over-45 and Over-50.

Yusuf thanked RC Manubhai and Apco Coatings for their continued support of veteran football in Fiji.

item.title: Naitasiri lead Skipper Cup points table after round 6
item.description: Naitasiri have collected 25 points from six matches, recording five wins and one loss. They have also produced an impressive +70 points differential, highlighting their strong performances so far in the competition.
item.content:encoded:
Naitasiri have collected 25 points from six matches, recording five wins and one loss.

They have also produced an impressive +70 points differential, highlighting their strong performances so far in the competition.

They are level on 25 points with Nadi and Tailevu, but Naitasiri sit in first place on points differential.

Nadi are second with five wins and one draw, while Tailevu are third with four wins and two draws.

Defending champions Malolo sit fourth on 23 points, followed by Nadroga on 22 points.

With the competition entering the crucial stages, Naitasiri will be looking to maintain their consistency and hold on to top spot as the race for the Skipper Cup title intensifies.

The fixture for this week are yet to be released.

item.title: OFC U-19 Men's Championship: Junior Bula Boys miss out on semi-finals after 2-1 loss to Tahiti
item.description: The Junior Bula Boys have missed out on a place in the semi-finals of the OFC Under-19 Men's Championship after losing 2-1 to Tahiti in their final Group B match in Samoa. Tahiti led 1-0 at half-time and extended its lead to 2-0 in the second half.
item.content:encoded:
The Junior Bula Boys have missed out on a place in the semi-finals of the OFC Under-19 Men's Championship after losing 2-1 to Tahiti in their final Group B match in Samoa.

Tahiti led 1-0 at half-time and extended its lead to 2-0 in the second half.

Fiji pulled one back through Abdullah Khairati, but Tahiti held on for the win.

Coach Marika Rodu congratulated Tahiti on the victory and said Fiji knew it would be a tough match for both teams.

Rodu says conceding early made the task difficult, but praised his players for continuing to stick together and fight for a way back into the match.

He says t he team had bonded well throughout the tournament and developed a strong level of belief.

He says the focus now is on improving and finishing the tournament in a positive manner.

Rodu says some players will be rested, while those who have had limited playing time will be given an opportunity in the team's final match.

He urged fans to continue supporting the team in their football journey.

The Junior Bula Boys are expected to face Papua New Guinea in the fifth-place playoff at 10am on Saturday.

item.title: Suva eyes fourth BOG title as they take on Ba FC in semi-final
item.description: Global Care Suva FC will be out to keep their Extra Battle of the Giants title hopes alive when they take on host Dayal’s Steel Ba FC in what promises to be an exciting first semi-final this Saturday. The Capital City side topped Group A after recording two wins from its three pool matches at the Four R Stadium at Govind Park in Ba.
item.content:encoded:
Global Care Suva FC will be out to keep their Extra Battle of the Giants title hopes alive when they take on host Dayal’s Steel Ba FC in what promises to be an exciting first semi-final this Saturday.

The Capital City side topped Group A after recording two wins from its three pool matches at the Four R Stadium at Govind Park in Ba.

Suva opened its campaign with a 3–1 win over Blue Gas Navua FC before producing a dominant performance to defeat defending champions Extra Supermarket Labasa FC 3–0.

Although the Whites suffered a 2–1 loss to Nasinu FC in their final pool match, their earlier results were enough to secure top spot in the group.

Suva coach Pita Rabo says Suva has shown confidence in attack, scoring seven goals during the pool stage.

However, they are expected to face a tougher test against a Ba side that will have the advantage of strong home support.

The Men in Black finished second in Group B after victories over Tagimoucia Nadi FC and Khelvin Realtors Lautoka FC, with their only defeat coming against group winner Stratum/PPCL Rewa FC.

Ba will head into the semi-final with confidence after a convincing 3–1 victory over Lautoka in its final pool match.

Suva, who have won the BOG title three times, will be determined to move a step closer to adding another trophy to its collection, while Ba will be hoping to make home-ground advantage count.

The first semi-final between Global Care Suva FC and Dayal’s Steel Ba FC will kick off at 2pm this Saturday at the Four R Stadium at Govind Park in Ba.
